prompt.en: Your toe touches something sharp, and within a moment the muscles of your leg pull your foot away. A message has to travel from your toe to those muscles. Describe how a neuron receives this kind of message and passes it on. Name the parts of the neuron in your answer.

level1.en: Which part of a neuron first takes in a signal?

clue.en: These are short branches at one end of the neuron. They receive signals from other neurons.

level2Template.en: A neuron receives a signal through its ___.

label.en: The axon carries the message away, over a long distance

level1.en: Which part of a neuron is a long fibre, and which way does it carry the message?

clue.en: This long fibre carries the message away from the cell body. It can reach far across the body.

level2Template.en: The message travels away from the cell body along the ___, a long fibre.

label.en: Axon terminals pass the message on to other cells

level1.en: Where does the axon end, and what happens to the message there?

clue.en: The axon ends in small branches. From them the message is passed to the next cell, such as a muscle.

level2Template.en: At the axon ___, the message is passed on to other cells such as muscle.

text.en: The dendrites of a neuron receive the signal.
The axon, a long fibre, carries the message away from the cell body, over a long distance.
The axon terminals pass the message on to other cells, such as the muscles of the leg.
